transcript.content: Jesus and Mary Chain, "Black," on XFM 104.9. It's ten past four. After the break, Oasis.
Muff Shandy says, "Turn it up. Earplugs are gay."
The new single by Muff Shandy, "Earplugs Are Gay."
It's the Ricky Gervais Show. Who am I, Steve?
Lucky you! Yes, it's me, Ricky Gervais!
Gervais, weren't you out signing autographs in the week?
Is this true, what I've heard?
Well, we did this roadshow from, er, the Doc Martens store.
Yeah. Me, Crowley and Pitts with, like, a CD player.
And, er, you played some records.
And people were coming up, weren't they, and asking for your— asking for your autograph.
Well you know I'm a bit of a celebrity, Steve, I'll be honest.
If you were really rich, what would you spend your money on?
You know what I spend my money on.
Just more food and drink than I do now.
How many people ask for autographs?
What about Crowley? Did you- did anyone ask, er, Crowley for an autograph?
No, they kept ask- asking him if they got this in a size seven.
He does look a bit like a sort of spotty shop assistant.
I'll just go and check with Maureen. Meantime, here's Idlewild.
We've— we're allowed to tell one joke, aren't we, a show?
One joke, because I don't want it to sound like, you know, Steve Penk. Or, you know.
No, no, it's terrible. No, nothing wrong with Steve Penk.
I'm a big fan of Penk.
Don't get me started on Penk.
If I start singing the praises of Penk, we'll be here all night.
But the point is, you know, you've got a gag, let's hear it.
A little boy, yeah, he's only five years old. He's lost in a busy high street and he's crying his eyes out. Well, he would. Lost his mummy.

He's going, "I've lost my—" A policeman comes up and, er, he goes, "All right, what's the matter?" He goes, "I've lost my mummy." Policeman said, "All right, don't worry, we'll find her. What's she like?" Little kid said, "Cock and bingo, mainly."
The Soundtrack of Our Lives - Instant Repeater '99
Instant repeater, 99, soundtrack of our lives on XFM 104.9.
Gervais, can I just give the listeners one very good reason why they should stay tuned? There are prizes up for grabs very soon. Another of your fantastic movie quizzes is on the way, Gervais.
Give me one reason why I should stay, then.
The stunning new single from Brainmangle, "Blood, Sweat and Cum."
"Blood, Sweat and Cum," by Brainmangle. Out now.
The new single from Velvet Nazi 666 UK is "[Bleep] Like a Rhino."
Velvet Nazi 666 UK - Fuck Like a Rhino
"[Bleep] Like a Rhino," from Velvet Nazi 666 UK. The UK is important.
Blur and "Tracy Jacks" on XFM 104.9. I really am a very good DJ.
Well, yeah, maybe. Er, 0171 580 2000. Do you agree with that statement? Is Ricky Gervais a very good DJ? Gervais, looking at the cover, the News of the World today—
I'm shocked. I mean, we all know. That, I mean, how are you coping? How are you getting through the days?
I'm— I'm in shock. I'm sort of pretending it hasn't happened. I'm playing a lot of the old records.
I know, I know exactly that, yeah. The Spice Girls are on the brink of splitting up.

Geri Halliwell has left the band, rumour has it, but even more worryingly, all right, apparently the reason Geri left was that she was bullied out of the group by Scary Spice. Apparently Scary Spice, Mel B, is absolutely vicious. Lots of, you know, lots of remarks about Geri.
Always sniping and going at her.
Well, this must be particularly close to your heart, because you were bullied at school by a pop star, weren't you?
Lionel Richie. Yeah. It was a nightmare. The thing was, Lionel had just left the Commodores.
And he had a lot of pent-up nervous energy, d'you know what I mean, which he just used to take out on me.
Take out on you. Because you looked gimp.
Well, it must've— must've worked, 'cause he was about to have, like, um, a big hit with "Dancing on the Ceiling."
Hold on, he'd have been flying high before that with Hello.
Well, exactly that. You see, the thing was, you know, he'd had a string of top 10 hits.
I was about 14. I didn't have the chart credibility with which to fight back.
D'you know what I mean? I mean, often he'd just be throwing my satchel in the tree, you know, er, and singing, "Hello, is it me you're looking for?"
What chance did you have against that?
How could I cope with that? You know, he's got a great singing voice. I haven't got soul, you know.
That is terrible. That is terrible.
But you had a similar problem, didn't you? Were you not bullied by a band?
That was before. I'm older than you. I mean, this was about twenty years ago when I was a kid at school.
And I was bullied by a whole band.
You were bullied by a whole band?
With the news that Geri Halliwell has left the Spice Girls, XFM has set up a helpline for distressed fans.
If you need a shoulder to cry on, call Ricky Gervais on 0171 580 2000.
I know. Andy, Andy, yep. Yep, I know, I know. Okay.

It's terrible. It's terrible. But, but listen, I want you to think of all the, um, the good, the good times she's given people. Um, the records that she was on still exist. Um, they'll always be there.
I can't believe it's gonna be the end of her career. She's a very, very talented young lady. And of course there's always the, uh, you know, the photos of her.
The photos on the internet. I'm not talking publicity. I'm talking filth. Yes.
I mean, there's one, right? It's- I don't know how they got away with it. She's got these- Hello? Hello? Well, anyway, she's got these two-
I'm not gonna lie to you. That was House of Pain and Jump Around.
Don't lie to me. Don't ever lie to me. Gervais.
No, that is House of Pain, "Jump Around." We were jumping around.
We've got no shame. XFM 104.9. It's 20 to 5.
I'll be honest. After the ad break, there'll be another record.
Is there gonna be another record?
There's gonna be an ad break?
Muff Shandy says, "Turn it up. Earplugs are gay."
The new single by Muff Shandy, "Earplugs Are Gay."
I really feel psyched up after that.
So do I. I just wanna— oh, you just saw me there. I was box— shadow-boxing again.
Good job Pitts was here. Because you can hit him as hard as you like and he can't feel it. Well, they feel it a couple of minutes later.
Yeah, it just sort of ripples.
It's great 'cause it takes out aggression. He sort of likes it 'cause it tickles him.
He's like... You remember Pillsbury Dough?
That little bloke that used to laugh when you used to prod him.
No idea what you're talking about.
0171 580 2000, everyone phone and say, Steve, you're a twat. Of course, I remember Pillsbury Doe, so don't try and do that one on me.
Right. Well, if that's the game you're playing, Gervais...
I'll try and pluck one out of the bag.
Oh, well, no, you can carry on talking. I'm just— mm, let me think, let me think.
No, I'll come up with something. I'll come up with something.
Does this involve a mate of yours in Bristol? Did you— do you know, er, you know Terry Wise? No?
No, I- I'll come up with something. So what, what was this thing? What was it called?
It was a little thing that used to come in, a little round wobbly thing, and you pressed him and you went...
Well, it's the name of a thing, innit? Pillsbury Dough!
What do you mean, a thing?
No! What, you used to play with food when you were a kid?
Gervais, you still play with food.
This is going nowhere. Shut up. No, forget it. Right, it's after the um, ad break...

Yeah, I remember that. Yeah. I remember that... What was that little kid in the comics that had the magic pipes? He'd go past an ad of, like, a woman eating a cream bun, and the cream bun would come to life.
You know what I mean? Now, at 14, he'd be getting different material, wouldn't he, to bring to life. Don't you remember him? He was in a comic book.
Oh, I love it when Grandad gets out of the bath. His skin's so clean and smooth.
But after a hard day squelching around, soreness can cause discomfort. New Panderers with [unclear] creamy caring stuff acts as a clunge protector.
And the new dry-weave chicken wings soak up all the piss and shit so Grandad stays dry. New Panderers with clunge protection. 'Cause I love my grandad.
Yeah, yeah, yeah, Gomez, yeah. Shut up, I've got to say what the record is. Gomez, get myself arrested. What, Steve?
I have finally figured out what on earth you were waffling on about just a second ago.
Right, you just, "Pillsbury Dough..." Apparently, I've managed— I'm talking to the listeners, Gervais, not yourself.
Apparently, Pillsbury Dough, right, it's an ad from years ago.
A little cartoon character comes on the telly, Pillsbury dough man.
And he comes on, and a woman presses his belly—
And he makes a noise or something?
Well you didn't say that at all!
You didn't explain it see when I want to explain something, alright Gervais, what I do is I think what do I need to say?
How can I best express it which words shall I use and in what order?
When you want to express something you just go, "Words, words, words, words, stop. Words, words. Oh, annoyed, annoyed words." D'you know what I mean? It's just cobbled together, Gervais.
I was excited about remembering Pillsbury Dough.
Yeah, but you, that, you must not let your excitement...
I couldn't believe— I couldn't believe you're so stupid and sheltered not to have heard of him.
You must not let your excitement right, undermine your use of grammar. Do you understand me, Gervais? It's not an excuse.
Anything, all right? Just think before you speak.
Think- please think before you speak.
Where would I get if I did that. Um, And someone here says, and. Starting off with and.
Never start a sentence with and or because. Gervais. Everybody knows that. Never start a sentence with and or because.
Mandy from Chingford wants to know if I remember a program called Billy Liar. Of course I do, you see. And you probably don't.
No, there's a film, I admit there's a film and a play and a book.
Happy birthday, Charlotte. No, Catherine. It's from Charlotte. She's 20.
Yeah, man, you're super slick on the mic. Oh, yes, sirree, Gervais.
Get me another one, get me another one. 'Cause the thing is, if you stop drinking, you start going a bit mad.
Can we, Can we get the margaritas in here, please, Nick?
Oh, I had a margarita yesterday, sitting outside a little restaurant in Camden, had a margarita.
Oh, I went to a party, I went to a party, I was on the Margaritas. Um, I saw one of 'em the next day, actually. She was a lovely girl.
No, you can't do jokes like that. What were we talking about before that, though?
Drugstore, sober on XFM 104.9, London's only alternative.
Interesting that you say that sentence every time we finish playing a record.
Because it's the only thing that you've memorised, isn't it?
You can actually say that and get from the beginning to the end without sort of keeling over or something.
Yeah, taking another swig. You should see him preparing to come out of a record. Right, XFM 104.9, and off you go. Yeah. It's beautiful, Gervais.
Absolutely gorgeous. Uh, Walking along um, the other night towards your house on that route, that direct route from XFM, walking along...
Very short fella walking alongside me, right and you know sometimes your eyes meet with these people. I saw his face.
What were you doing, crawling how short are we talking?
I saw his face. It looked— you know those people that look as though their face has been stapled together?
He was one of those sort of people.
And so his face, very odd. I mean, you know, I, I don't want to sort of, er, it's a bit like the pot calling the kettle black.
D'you know what I mean? But he was—
He was short and ugly, you're tall and ugly.
But he was— he was a weird-looking fella.
He looks up at me, Gervais. He looks up at me and he says, er, "Can I jump on your back?"
Absolutely what he said. Can you believe that? "Can I jump on your back?" What was I gonna say? It's ridiculous.
Can I jump on your back and I don't know what his plan, once he's got up there, I'm not sure what his plan of action was going to be. I don't know what he was thinking.
Yeah. Um, anyway, he says— says that, and I say, "Well, no, you can't." And he says, "Oh, go on, let me, you big C-U-N-T."
That’s what he said! “Oh, go on, let me!” I mean, it’s ridiculous. Absolutely ridiculous.
Like that was going to convince you.
At first sight: "Oh, well, no, I won't." "Oh, go on, you big—" "Oh, go on, then."
What if it had been a short, ugly woman who'd had her face stapled together?
Well, I'd have let her jump up.
Well, she might have needed to get somewhere quick. You know, those kind of opportunities. It would just be ungentlemanly.
She might have needed a ride.
She might have needed a ride.
After the break, a classic by the Housemartins.
No, just called Happy Hour. Don't embarrass yourself, you swine.
Why did you play that then? That was your choice for today. Go on.
Well, I'll tell you why I played that. It reminds me of a girl. No seriously.
What, you went out with a girl.
We played that song quite a lot.
Don't mock, don't judge you know.
But she was— she was, this is absolutely true, she was very odd.
She used to, she used to decide everything.
She would write out— she would tear a piece of paper in half, and she would write, you know, yes or no. Like, it might— her question to herself—
You know she had two no's in her hand, don't you?
Every night she had two noes.
Her question might have been, "Should we go down the supermarket?" Yes, no.
You know, and she'd, she'd, you know, choose one—
At random. No, won't go down the supermarket. She might have, you know, "Shall I buy a new hat?"
She might have yes, no, choose a paper, no. And, er, you know, she's just a bit odd, just a bit weird. And no, and that is exactly how, er, it all finished.
Yeah. She did— she wrote, you know, she made the— the question she asked herself was—
Is this true, by the way.
The question she asked herself was, shall I carry on going out with Steve?
Piece of paper: yes, no. No. That's— d'you know what I mean, that's quite a tragic story.
Best out of three, she kept saying.
That is tragic. I mean that really is quite tragic.
It makes me quite— it makes me a love martyr, doesn't— don't you think?
It was so much more, because you can put it down to, like, fate and luck now, as opposed to, you know...
Yeah. Yeah. It was the gods.
Well, if you're listening, this was your tune. This is the Delgado's Everything Goes Around.

You know, but I'm a little bit worried.

Well it is juvenile, yeah I mean that's the point. It's juvenile and silly and it's not particularly clever, but it is f***ing funny.
What? Um... what did you say then?
It's— I'm just saying, it is, you're right. You know, it is sort of juvenile and childish a bit as well, but it's f***ing funny, isn't it? And that's the important thing.
How did you— how did you do that? How d'you— is that some kind of wind-up?
And it's and it's being bleeped out.
Of course it is. It's radio.
Well how are you doing it then?
Is it- is it a wind-up? Is it some...
Yeah, of course it's f***ing live XFM 104.9 London's only f***ing alternative.
Well, can I swear? If I swear, would it do the same?
Well, I don't know. It's your... Take a chance. It's your neck on the line.
You can't go around saying big hairy dog's c***.
If you swear again, Steve, um, I'm serious, I'll be annoyed 'cause you're making me look like a w***er. This is Radiohead and "Black Star."
Radiohead and "Black Star" on XFM 104.9. It's the Ricky Gervais Show. We've had the competition.

Gervais, you know, it's been great. We've enjoyed ourselves.

Oh, the film, of course. We didn't even give it away. It was Terminator 2.

It's a fantastic clip there from the film and hopefully another film quiz next week. Perhaps.
